matches.d: About TJM Labs TJM Labs is building the digital workforce for pharmacy. Pharmacies are being asked to do more with fewer resources. Prescription volumes are growing, margins are tightening, and talented pharmacy teams spend too much of their day on repetitive operational work. We're changing that. TJM Labs builds AI-powered automation designed specifically for pharmacy. Our technology works within the systems pharmacies already use to automate repetitive workflows and create more capacity for pharmacists and pharmacy technicians to focus on the work that actually requires them. We're growing quickly, and successful implementation is one of the most important parts of delivering on that promise. That's where you come in. About the Role We're looking for an Implementation Lead to own the day-to-day execution of customer implementations from discovery through go-live and transition to ongoing support. This is a hands-on role at the intersection of pharmacy operations, project management, customer communication, and technology. You'll work in close partnership with a Customer Success Manager (CSM). The CSM owns the overall customer relationship, strategic alignment, and escalations. You own getting the implementation done. During implementation, you'll be the hub of the project. You'll coordinate customer and internal stakeholders, document how the pharmacy operates today, translate those workflows into clear requirements, maintain the implementation plan, manage communication and action items, own internal QA, and drive the project toward a successful go-live. You'll also own one of the most important safeguards in our implementation process: making sure what the pharmacy does, what we've documented, what we've asked our technical teams to build, and what we ultimately deliver all remain in sync. This isn't a role where you'll simply maintain a project plan and schedule meetings. You'll ask questions. You'll uncover exceptions. You'll document details. You'll chase down decisions. You'll test what we've built. You'll notice when something doesn't line up. You'll keep people accountable for commitments. And when a project starts drifting, you'll help get it back on course. You don't need to be an engineer or an AI expert. You do need to understand pharmacy operations and pharmacy management systems, be curious about technology, communicate exceptionally well, and be very good at turning complexity into clarity. What You'll Own 1. Day-to-Day Implementation Execution Once a customer enters implementation, you'll own the day-to-day work required to get them live. Establish and maintain the implementation plan, milestones, dependencies, and target go-live date. Lead implementation meetings, discovery sessions, and working sessions. Coordinate activities across the pharmacy, TJM technical teams, the CSM, and other internal stakeholders. Track decisions, action items, customer deliverables, risks, dependencies, and outstanding requirements. Follow up consistently to keep projects moving. Identify risks and blockers early and drive them toward resolution. Manage implementation changes and understand their impact on scope, requirements, and timelines. Keep projects on schedule and surface concerns before they become surprises. Coordinate go-live activities and the transition into ongoing support. At any point in the project, you should be able to answer: What needs to happen next to get this customer live? 2. Pharmacy Process Discovery & Documentation Before we can automate a pharmacy workflow, we need to understand exactly how that workflow operates today. You'll own creating and maintaining clear, accurate, and highly standardized documentation of each customer's current-state pharmacy processes before TJM automation is introduced. Lead structured workflow discovery with pharmacy stakeholders. Understand how work moves through the pharmacy today — including people, pharmacy management systems, other technology, handoffs, business rules, decision points, and dependencies. Document current-state processes using TJM's standard formats, terminology, and required level of detail. Capture exceptions and edge cases, not just the ideal or 'happy path.' Ask the follow-up questions needed to uncover assumptions, inconsistencies, and missing information. Validate documented workflows with the customer. Keep documentation current as new information is discovered or requirements change. Ensure important changes are reflected consistently across process documentation, requirements, implementation work, and testing. Help define how workflows should operate once TJM automation is introduced. Maintain a clear connection between how the pharmacy operates today, what the customer needs, and what TJM ultimately builds. Good documentation in this role isn't about writing more. It's about capturing the right information, in the right structure, so customers and TJM teams are operating from the same understanding. 3. Requirements & Technical Translation You'll help translate real-world pharmacy operations into clear requirements our technical teams can act on. You won't need to arrive as a technical business analyst, and you won't be expected to write code. We'll teach you TJM's technology, tools, and implementation methodology. Translate operational workflows into structured, actionable requirements. Identify relevant business rules, dependencies, expected outcomes, exceptions, and edge cases. Give technical teams the context they need to understand both what needs to happen and why. Answer questions and close gaps that arise as technical work progresses. Review proposed solutions against documented customer workflows and requirements. Identify when something being built doesn't appear to match what was documented or agreed upon. Keep requirements and documentation aligned as the implementation evolves. One of your most important responsibilities is preventing quiet drift between what the pharmacy needs, what we've documented, and what we're building. 4. Stakeholder Communication & Alignment You'll own communication across all stakeholders involved in the implementation. During implementation, you are the primary day-to-day implementation contact for the customer and the internal hub for project information. Establish and maintain a clear communication cadence. Lead customer implementation meetings and internal project discussions. Provide clear, concise updates on progress, timelines, decisions, risks, blockers, and next steps. Ensure decisions and changes are documented and communicated to everyone they affect. Make sure customer feedback and requirements reach the appropriate internal teams. Make sure internal decisions and updates make their way back to the appropriate customer stakeholders. Clearly communicate owners, commitments, and deadlines. Keep the CSM informed of project health, customer sentiment, risks, and important developments. Bring in the CSM when an issue requires strategic, relationship, commercial, or executive intervention. You own making sure the right people know the right things at the right time. 5. Internal QA & Customer Readiness You'll own the quality gate between work produced internally and what is presented to the customer. Customers should never be the first people to discover that something we built doesn't work as expected. Develop a clear understanding of what 'working correctly' means for each implementation. Validate completed work against documented customer requirements and workflows. Coordinate and execute internal testing before customer review. Test expected workflows as well as relevant exceptions and edge cases. Document defects, unexpected behavior, and gaps clearly enough for technical teams to act on them. Track identified issues through resolution. Retest fixes and confirm that previously identified issues have actually been resolved. Ensure the implementation reflects agreed-upon requirements and documented process changes. Determine when work is ready to move from internal QA to customer validation. Coordinate customer testing after internal QA is complete. Track customer feedback and issues through final resolution and go-live readiness. You don't need to be a software QA engineer. You do need to be methodical, curious, detail-oriented, and willing to test something until you're confident we're putting quality work in front of the customer. Your responsibility isn't simply to ask whether something was tested. It's to make sure we're confident in what we're asking the customer to test. 6. Continuous Improvement Implementation playbooks and processes. Pharmacy workflow documentation standards. Templates and project tools. Discovery practices. Requirements documentation. Internal QA and testing processes. Go-live readiness. Customer and internal communication. Handoffs between implementation and ongoing Customer Success. The goal isn't simply to complete implementations. It's to make our implementation process more consistent, predictable, efficient, and scalable every time we use it. You'll Probably Love This Role If... You get unusual satisfaction from turning chaos into a plan. You leave meetings knowing exactly who is doing what by when — and you've written it down. You notice the unanswered question everyone else skipped over. When someone says, 'and then we just process it normally,' your instinct is to ask, 'Okay, but what exactly does normally mean?' You understand that the way a workflow is supposed to happen and the way it actually happens at 4:45 on a Friday afternoon aren't always the same thing. You test things yourself instead of assuming that because someone said they're done, they're ready for the customer. You'd rather solve a problem than spend three days discussing who owns it. You like technology, but you're more interested in what it can do than technology for technology's sake. Why TJM Labs You'll join a fast-growing company working on a very real problem in healthcare.

matches.d: About Kaseya Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success. Backed by Insight Partners , a leading global software investor, Kaseya has experienced sustained double-digit growth and continues to expand its global footprint. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide. Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in engineering, product, sales, marketing, customer support, or operations, your work helps protect, defend, and optimize IT environments across the globe. We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in. At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it. Position Summary The Business Process Lead, Digital & Service Experience owns the end-to-end design of our customer-facing digital and service experience — commerce, account self-service, our customer and partner portal, and the service function that supports customers across those channels. This position carries both live operational ownership of processes running in production today and the design and build of a genuine product-led digital commerce capability that does not yet exist. What exists today is an account and billing self-service surface; building an actual product-led commerce motion — trials, in-app purchase, and self-serve upgrade — is the central mandate of this role. Importantly, this role owns the business capabilities in this scope — their definition, design, decomposition, and governance — in close partnership with the business teams that operate the underlying functions day to day. It does not own those functions themselves; success depends on heavy partnership with business and technology leads rather than on direct authority. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role: the person hired personally facilitates working sessions, maps processes, writes requirements, and stays engaged through delivery and adoption. It also sits within a newly created function whose standards are still being defined, and is a strong opportunity for someone who wants to build a practice rather than execute within an established one. Because this role spans live operational processes with service-level expectations attached and net-new capability design with no existing internal playbook, it requires someone comfortable holding both kinds of work simultaneously and deliberately protecting time for design work even when operational demands feel more urgent. Key Responsibilities Own and continuously maintain a detailed (L2/L3) decomposition of account self-service, portal, commerce, and service-experience capabilities, keeping documentation accurate as the operating model and systems landscape evolve, and using standards shared across the Business Process Lead team. Facilitate structured working sessions with the digital team and Customer Success leadership to document how processes work today and design how they should work going forward, producing process maps, documented decisions, and requirements a technical team can act on without extensive follow-up. Translate future-state process designs into system requirements, partner with Product Owners and Engineering Leads through design, build, and testing, and confirm that what gets delivered reflects the intended process design. Support two parallel delivery tracks — current, in-production systems and the next-generation platform build — correctly identifying which track an incoming request belongs to, and ensuring lessons learned in day-to-day operations are reflected back into documentation and forward-looking design work. Own change management, enablement, and adoption for process changes in this value stream — stakeholder impact assessment, readiness planning, training materials, and post-launch verification that new processes are being used as intended — and define and report the process performance metrics that show whether they are working. Hold and maintain documented agreements at shared boundaries with peer Business Process Leads, so handoffs between value streams are explicitly agreed rather than assumed. Design the target digital commerce operating model — which products, customer segments, and transaction types become available for self-service purchase and in what sequence — and the business process behind new product-led motions including trials, in-app purchase, and self-serve upgrade, resolving eligibility, entitlement, pricing enforcement, and approval logic before anything is built. Maintain a capability-level build plan that sequences dependencies against the other BIS value streams so digital and core system readiness arrive together, explicitly defining whether and when an assisted process is retired once a digital capability supersedes it, and own the capability design for the customer service experience in partnership with Customer Success and Support leadership. Required Qualifications Direct experience building or scaling a self-serve commerce or product-led growth motion — trial-to-paid conversion, in-product purchase, or self-serve upgrade — including funnel instrumentation and conversion measurement. Experience limited to account or billing self-service portal work, or to general process documentation without direct commerce-building experience, is not sufficient for this role. 5+ years of experience in business process design, business analysis, business architecture, or operations in a relevant domain. Demonstrated experience decomposing business capabilities into detailed, multi-level structures. Strong facilitation skills with cross-functional business stakeholders, including experience working at a director level. Experience translating business process requirements into system requirements for a technical delivery team, along with strong documentation habits. Preferred Qualifications Direct experience standing up a new digital commerce or product-led motion within a business that previously sold only through an assisted sales model. Trial design and trial-to-paid conversion experience, including eligibility, entitlement, and conversion instrumentation. Digital product or eCommerce product management experience, including running experiments and iterative product releases. Support operations and case deflection design experience, including knowledge management and escalation design. Identity, login, and profile management experience in a customer-facing digital product, and account or billing self-service portal operations experience. Familiarity with structured change management methodologies and prioritization frameworks such as WSJF or RICE. Experience with Salesforce B2B Commerce, Salesforce Service Cloud and case management, Experience Cloud community platforms, and payment gateway integrations. Additional information Kaseya provides equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, age, ancestry, gender, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

matches.d: We are a team of consultants solving a familiar problem: how do you earn credibility with a client? We believe it starts with understanding the client’s industry. Modern business has become the Tower of Babel: every industry has its own language. If you speak your client's language, you connect and find a way in. And if you don’t, you’re flying blind with a surface-level understanding. Companies spend millions on dull, slow, and unscalable solutions. The traditional go-tos – SMEs, in-house content, and live training – aren’t working. We created a new way to learn an industry in under an hour (imagine the “I know kung fu” scene from The Matrix , but for business), using fun animated stories produced like a media product. Our primers are widely used by the world's top consulting and technology firms, with 90%+ completion rates, rave reviews, and hundreds of deals won and projects delivered. Primerli is scaling fast, which means every process we have is up for a rethink. We are on a transformation journey to AI-native ways of working, which makes this a genuinely exciting time to join. If you're curious, resourceful, and ready to roll up your sleeves and make things happen, this role is for you. The Role This role works with every team in the business. You will report to the Head of Operations and support Sales, Customer Success, and Product. Your first job is to keep the engine running: product delivery, client onboarding, data reporting, and admin processes. But there’s more to it - you’ll reinvent how we get work done alongside AI agents, and write the playbook for how Primerli operates. And when strategic problems pop up, you’ll help us crack them. This is an ideal role for someone early in their career who enjoys moving between strategy and execution, would rather solve problems than follow a checklist, and wants to learn how an AI-native company works. About Primerli Primerli is a bootstrapped, early stage start-up that created the first and only engaging way to learn an industry in under an hour. We serve over 2 million professionals at global enterprises including MBB, Big Four, Google, and Microsoft. Get a feel for it yourself – check out our sample videos on YouTube:. We are a small team with big ambitions. Many of us came from consulting backgrounds and joined Primerli because we wanted to move beyond advising to building. At a company of our size, you will get real ownership early, work closely with leadership, and help drive the direction of the business. If you’re looking to make a meaningful impact and grow alongside the company, this is the kind of role where that can happen. What You'll Do Mandate Keep Primerli running smoothly and efficiently, and work cross-functionally to solve the company’s most important problems. Responsibilities Business Operations (50%) Own the recurring workflows that keep clients happy: onboarding, course delivery, NASBA compliance Build dashboards and reporting to track business health and product usage Help key enterprise clients troubleshoot technical issues Problem Solving (40%) Turn the workflows you run into AI agents and automations, then keep making them better Help shape how all of Primerli uses AI: shared tools, workflows, and a company knowledge base Special Projects (10%) Contribute to projects that shape how Primerli operates and scales (e.g., analyze build vs. partner options for technology investments) What We're Looking For Values & Attitude High agency and ownership: You don't wait to be told. You spot problems nobody assigned to you, grab them, and follow through without reminders. Low ego, growth mindset: You ask for feedback, take it well, and act on it. The best idea wins, even when it isn't yours. Strong values: You care about others, not just yourself, and you see competitiveness as complementary, not a barrier, to showing compassion, kindness, and empathy. Get-stuff-done attitude: You are energized by action, and can balance priorities and timelines. You know when to be fast and scrappy and when to slow down and get things right.‍ Experience & Skills Bachelor's degree in a STEM field Experience building with AI tools Client-facing experience (consulting club or internship counts) Strong analytical skills and data fluency Clear and professional written communication Nice-to-have Experience working in a high-growth environment 1-2 years of management consulting experience at a top-tier firm Interest in learning, teaching, or education What You'll Get Competitive salary: $100-150k base, plus bonus Medical and dental health coverage 401k contributions and profit sharing PTO and paid leave for parents Location and Work Environment While the company is based in California, you will work remotely with a global team. We are open to candidates based in the United States and Canada. Candidates must be comfortable working with colleagues in different time zones and traveling up to 10% of the time to co-locate with the team. Originally posted on Himalayas

PerfectServe now has 400+ employees, 30,000+ customers — spanning medical practices, hospitals, and health systems — and $100 million+ in annual revenue. PerfectServe’s mission is to accelerate speed to care by optimizing provider schedules and routing communications — including messages, pages, calls, and alerts — to the right place at the right time in any care setting. By facilitating real-time information sharing, building better schedules, and automating important clinical workflows, we believe we can help our customers advance patient care and improve the well-being of their clinicians. About the Role Come help us redefine last-mile logistics through robotics, automation, and other advanced technologies. Autonomy only works when merchants — restaurants, retailers, and other partners — can reliably interact with our robots: handing off orders, troubleshooting edge cases, and trusting the experience enough to keep using it. matches.d: Location: Remote, New York City, or Oakland Travel is encouraged approximately once every 6 months to state partners within the continental USA, and occasionally required. We expect these trips to include visits to prisons and parole offices. Role Type: Full-time Compensation : $120,000 Visa sponsorship: Not available Hires remotely in: United States Experience: 5+ years of full-time, professional work experience Recidiviz is thrilled to be hiring a Senior Policy Data Analyst to join our team! We’re a small, fast-moving group that works with complex criminal justice data from our state partners and develops analyses and tools that target the drivers of incarceration. That’s where you come in. We’re looking for someone who has creativity and inquisitiveness to identify and solve open-ended problems, clarity to think through complex and variable data, flexibility to adjust in a rapidly evolving environment, and above all else, a collaborative, kind nature to add to our culture. About us Recidiviz is creating safer, healthier communities by improving outcomes for people in the criminal justice system. We build technology to reduce the number of people in prison and to help criminal justice leaders embrace data-driven decision-making. Using software tools and thoughtful product design, we’ve been able to safely and permanently reduce incarceration and improve outcomes. We work side-by-side with leaders of the criminal justice system, people in prison and on supervision, and ecosystem partners to build a better path forward. In addition to the revenue we earn from state partners, some of the most respected philanthropists and foundations support our work. People who succeed at Recidiviz lead with kindness and humility, assume good intent, learn from failure, and fix problems when they see them. They are excited to work arm in arm with government leadership and staff to improve outcomes. They are great listeners. They build deep relationships with and empathy for the people we work with and the people who our mission serves, even when those two groups feel at odds. About the role Recidiviz's policy team works with state DOC leaders who want to rewrite old policies or write new ones, grounded in evidence and analytics, to improve outcomes. We use administrative datasets to generate context-responsive insights that expand momentum for policy change. We answer questions like: What earned sentence credit structure creates the strongest reward system given the distribution of sentence lengths and program availability? How do the factors that drive parole board decisions align with the factors most quantitatively predictive of post-release outcomes? How would outcomes change if dynamic factors were weighted more heavily? How will a new supervision contact standard affect the alignment between supervision officer bandwidth and high-need clients? By translating policy concepts into concrete modeling, we help states make smarter and more ambitious changes. Senior Policy Data Analysts are high-autonomy technical contributors. They own an end to end analytic process — breaking project objectives into analytical products, designing the approach, derisking the timeline, producing the findings, and preparing the materials that go in front of decision-makers. The core skill is decision-support: building analysis for a decision rather than for a research finding. This role is as much about making judgment calls as it is about running analytical work. Most of our projects are first of their kind, which requires designing the approach as you go. Projects change mid-flight as our understanding of system dynamics develops and the needs of stakeholders shift. This role works closely with a Partnerships Lead, who coordinates with state partners to determine project objectives. The Senior Policy Data Analyst sets the analysis strategy to meet those objectives. Success is measured by the impact your interventions drive. Core responsibilities Building analysis from corrections and parole data . You'll use SQL and Python to wrangle administrative data to articulate how a system behaves. You ramp up on new data quickly, going deep where it changes the answer and making defensible simplifying assumptions where it doesn’t. Modeling policy scenarios and quantifying tradeoffs . Apply statistical methods like regressions, time series, stock-and-flow modeling or distributional analysis to project how outcomes change under different policy designs, and assess what the data can and can't support. A core judgment is developing simple and elegant approaches that cut to the heart of the decision point. Communicating findings to the people making the decision . You work backward from what information a stakeholder needs to advance decision-making in the room. You'll create the decks and memos that go to DOC leadership, find the frameworks that make a complicated tradeoff digestible, and take responsibility for tailoring your work to the audience to motivate action . Running your projects end to end . You'll translate project objectives into an analysis strategy, set project roadmaps, and identify and address unknowns. You’ll adjust course as project objectives change, and rightsize analysis with impact. Collaborating across Recidiviz . You'll collaborate across the organization to obtain state context, understand underlying data infrastructure, and support policy implementation. Finding the next opportunity. You’ll go deeper on the states you work in — spotting where additional analysis could unlock a decision, and running the early exploration to assess whether it’s worth pursuing. Wild success A year from now: You've driven impact . Your work has directly shaped several policy reforms across the country. You’ve uncovered new opportunities. You spotted a new opportunity in your states that became new work for the team. You've made your projects more effective. The people around you have less scramble, clearer ownership, and smoother handoffs, making it easier for everyone to focus on driving towards impact. You've leveled up our analytical team . Approaches you designed, like a modeling pattern or a framework for a recurring question, are now being reused by teammates on other states. Minimum qualifications 5 or more years of practical experience exploring, analyzing, and processing complex datasets Professional experience using SQL with large datasets, including high proficiency writing efficient queries for complex extraction and transformation Professional experience with Python, particularly pandas, for statistical analysis and data visualization Sufficient statistical background to reason about analysis design, examine results closely, and prepare analyses that hold up to scrutiny Experience scoping and delivering analytical work — particularly balancing depth and speed when navigating short timelines and shifting priorities Experience on teams where ownership is shared across functions, including proactively seeking context you're missing and flagging risks before they become blockers. matches.why: Global Program Manager role at a premier AI biotech SaaS company, fitting your program delivery strengths well.
matches.d: We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era. When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done. Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma. We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today. ROLE OVERVIEW Benchling is seeking an experienced customer-facing Global Program Manager (GPM) to oversee the post-sale experience for our largest Enterprise customers. The GPM will partner closely with the Enterprise Account Executive to ensure that customers achieve rapid time to value and see the value in expanding their relationship with Benchling as they transform and modernize their R&D IT. The GPM will coordinate implementation, customer success, and customer support efforts to ensure customers have a seamless experience post-sale. The GPM must have deep experience in Life Sciences R&D processes and scientific concepts as well as operating in an enterprise SaaS environment and be adept at working with internal and external stakeholders at all levels. RESPONSIBILITIES - Oversee post-sale activities across implementation, support, customer success, and optimization services for one or more more Enterprise customers - Partner with customer leaders and Benchling account teams to develop implementation, governance, change management, risk management, escalation management, adoption, and success plans that accelerate customer digital transformations - Liaise with customer leaders and be known as a diplomatic, pragmatic partner, who operates with sense of urgency to effect a best in class customer experience - Partner with the Enterprise AE to ensure seamless customer experience and grow the account - Support the development of customer experience sales proposals and other services proposals with account, and/or program subject matter expertise - Coordinate all Professional Services, Customer Success and Support activities to drive customer value, adoption, and advocacy - Partner with Product Management to maintain strategic engagement and alignment of customer needs with product roadmap - You will help shape the long-term strategy and vision for the Enterprise services business - You will inspire your cross-functional account team to accelerate our growth within the world’s largest biopharma companies by delivering exceptional customer experiences - You will be seen as a trusted advisor who has the customer’s best interests in mind, even when it means having a hard conversation - You will mentor, coach, and champion your cross-functional account team as you help them grow their professional skills - You will contribute meaningfully to running a profitable services business that doesn’t sacrifice quality or customer success in doing so - You will be a respected cross-functional partner to our Sales, Solutions, and Product teams, known for fairly advocating for both the customer and for Benchling QUALIFICATIONS Must haves: - Passionate about and experience working with Life Sciences companies with an understanding of R&D processes and scientific concepts. Must be able to confidently engage and build trust with scientific, informatics, IT, and Director/VP level audiences in top-20 Biotech and Pharma companies. - You are accountable and able to thrive in a fast-paced environment. You have strong executive presence and succeed in a matrixed environment where you have accountability without authority. - At least 10+ years client facing implementation, program leadership and/or consulting experience, with demonstrated record of successfully running large scale programs, ideally in the Life Sciences or Biotechnology sponsor or software space. - Proven ability to lead large cross-functional post-sale teams to deliver transformational change with superior relationship, project management, organizational, and commercial skills. This includes work across professional services, customer support, customer success, product, marketing, strategy, and sales. - Experienced in program and project management for multi-workstream enterprise SaaS deployments including scope management, budget control, project and executive reporting, and project financials. - Experience in services commercials including SOWs, budgeting, resourcing, and change orders. - Excellent interpersonal skills in verbal, written and presentation formats and experience presenting to the C-suite. - Ability to work at customer site, or in the Boston office based on customer and project needs. - BS or advanced degree in Biology, Molecular Biology, Genetics, Biotechnology, Bioengineering or similar life science field preferred, or equivalent professional experience working with Life Sciences R&D processes and/or healthcare technology. Nice to have: - GxP experience including software validation (CSV) at a life sciences or biotech company and/or vertical SaaS software company. HOW WE WORK We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday). #LI-Hybrid #BI-Hybrid #LI-SF1 Benchling welcomes everyone. We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences. We are an equal opportunity employer. That means we don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible. 🚀 Engagement Management is a new and fast-growing practice at ClickUp, and it's quickly becoming central to how we serve our enterprise customers. Our EMs bring program leadership, service delivery and change management together in one role. As a ClickUp Senior Engagement Manager you will lead the formation and orchestration of post-sale strategy and execution for the company’s largest and most strategic clients. We're looking for someone hungry, who excels in building, and who takes genuine pride in the quality of their work. Here, Engagement Managers are the single point of accountability for outcomes. You own everything between the contract being signed and the client seeing measurable results: what was sold gets delivered, on time and on margin, and we can prove it worked. You'll lead enterprise SaaS implementations across the full engagement lifecycle, from shaping scope in pre-sales, mobilizing the team and delivery, go-live, stabilization and a clean handover to the account team. You'll run work-stream programs with Paid TAMs, AI specialists, Product and Engineering, and the client's own project team, and you'll be the trusted advisor to the client's executive sponsor. Simply put: you are the single point of accountability for delivery, the client's partner in getting value from ClickUp, and a thought leader for how we deliver. YOUR ROLE - Stakeholder Management - Serve as the primary client contact for delivery - Build strong relationships with stakeholders while ensuring delivery remains aligned to client objectives and contractual commitments. - Build trusted relationships with client executive sponsors and program leads at VP and C-level, acting as their primary point of contact for delivery. - Navigate complex enterprise stakeholder environments and competing priorities across client functions (IT, PMO, business sponsors, procurement) and broker alignment when they conflict. - Project Delivery Oversight - Deliver engagements against agreed scope, schedule, hours budget and quality, using rigorous change control to protect timelines and delivery margin. - Translate customer business requirements into internal deliverables and milestones - Own engagement governance, including kickoffs, weekly working sessions, sponsor check-ins and SteerCos, and provide clear, concise status reporting to clients and internal stakeholders. - Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary teams, fostering a collaborative, accountable and high-performing delivery culture while providing coaching, direction and support. - Proactively manage risks, issues and dependencies through the RAID log, and act as the primary escalation point. - Manage engagement financials, including hours burn, forecasting, utilisation and margin, flagging overrun risk early and agreeing recovery plans. - Drive AI adoption - Guide clients from manual workflows to AI-assisted and agent-driven operations, and own post-go-live adoption outcomes. - Drive Value and Business Outcomes - Identify expansion opportunities through delivery and co-sell with Account Executives, bringing the delivery credibility that secures follow-on work. - Establish a value baseline before configuration begins, track benefits through go-live, and produce the value assessment that underpins renewal and expansion. - Governance - Design and run governance mechanisms - Track delivery efficacy, timelines, value realization and customer experience - Create continuous-improvement mechanisms - Change Management & Communication - Own communications around delivery status, risks and outcomes - Manage escalation and communication across customer/internal teams - Assess change readiness and resistance across impacted teams; build sponsor and champion networks to carry the rollout. - Design the communications and enablement plan with the client, and sequence go-live to match the organization's capacity for change. - Role Development - Contribute to building the Engagement Management practice by iterating on templates, playbooks and AI workflows that make every engagement faster and more consistent. YOUR SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE - 5+ years of software and/or services delivery experience, with at least 2 years as the accountable project, program or engagement lead. - Proven track record taking enterprise SaaS deployments from kickoff through go-live and into adoption, ideally in work management, PSA, CRM, ITSM or collaboration platforms. - Strong grasp of SaaS implementation fundamentals: workspace and data architecture, permissions and SSO, integrations, data migration, change management and enablement. No coding required, but you can challenge an unrealistic technical scope. - Comfortable with Agile, Waterfall and hybrid delivery, and knowing which one the client actually needs. - Commercial acumen: you've managed engagement budgets, SoWs, change requests and margin, and you know when to push for expansion vs when to stabilize. - Executive presence: you can run a SteerCo, deliver bad news early with a recovery plan, and hold a line on scope with a CIO in the room. - Experience leading cross-functional and distributed teams you don't directly manage, across client, partner and internal resources. - Strategic judgment to separate genuine product gaps from client process or training gaps. - Hands-on with AI: you already use AI to work faster, and you can credibly advise clients on where agents and automation fit. - Excellent written and verbal communication. Status reports people actually read. Nice to have: Experience in work management or SaaS software, professional services firms, agencies or regulated industries. PMP Certification. WHAT YOU'LL LOVE ABOUT WORKING HERE - Impact: Lead high-visibility enterprise engagements with global brands, and see the result in their day-to-day work. - Build something: Engagement Management is a new function. You'll help define the methodology, tooling and AI workflows that become the standard. - AI at the centre: Work on the frontier of AI-driven work management, with ClickUp Brain and Super Agents in your own delivery toolkit. - Career growth: A clear path from Engagement Manager to Senior or Principal Engagement Manager. - Community: Learn alongside Paid TAMs, AI specialists and delivery leaders across EMEA and NA. Able to turn business needs into technical solutions. - AI-Native: Demonstrated experience designing and scaling AI-powered workflows, agents and automations, not just using AI tools. Skilled at identifying and scoping AI use cases and consumption plans. - Consultative Discovery: Excellent at workflow analysis, process design and finding friction points. Uses structured discovery to map customer needs into scalable solutions. - Project & Program Management: Manages complex customer programs with multiple stakeholders, deadlines and outcomes. matches.why: Target BizOps lead role at a well-funded clean energy platform with strong pay, though slightly senior on the years of experience asked.
matches.d: WE’RE SUPERCHARGING THE CLEAN ECONOMY Crux is the capital markets platform changing the way clean energy and manufacturing projects are financed in the U.S. Crux’s platform, market intelligence, and expert team help developers and manufacturers unlock financing through all stages of project development and operation. Our team of 120+ is composed of experts in energy, tax, finance, government, and technology. We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Overture, Ardent Venture Partners, QED, Canapi, and others. These funds are joined by strategic investors including Pattern Energy, Clearway Energy, EDF Renewables, Intersect Power, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures. AN INFLECTION POINT IN AMERICAN ENERGY AND MANUFACTURING Energy demand is growing for the first time in 20 years, driven by surging manufacturing, transportation, electrification, and data centers. Simultaneously, hundreds of billions of dollars are being invested in domestic supply chains for critical minerals and components. Developers and manufacturers will require trillions of dollars in capital to meet growing needs. Unfortunately, the capital markets supporting this transformation remain opaque, fragmented, and complex. At Crux, we recognized the missing infrastructure: a central capital markets platform designed specifically for the next century of American energy and industry. By connecting counterparties, providing market intelligence, and streamlining transactions, we unlock faster decision making, lower cost of capital, and accelerated investment. THE ROLE We are hiring a BizOps Lead to design and deploy automation-first infrastructure in our Capital Solutions Business Execution team. This role is tailored for a problem-solver who blends a deep understanding of financial and diligence operations with a tool-savvy mindset, someone who’s excited to identify bottlenecks, automate manual processes, and craft robust internal systems that help Crux scale. About the role We’re looking for someone to join our Sales Strategy & Operations team and own how ElevenLabs goes to market by vertical. Be the single thread that keeps every function moving in the same direction. - Product Needs - Dig deep into what each vertical requires from the product — integrations, compliance, features, workflows, and translate field signal into prioritized, evidence-backed requirements for Product. - Data-Driven Strategy - Define the metrics that matter for each vertical (pipeline, win rate, ACV, sales cycle, product adoption), build the dashboards, and use the insights to decide where to double down or pull back. - Leadership Partnership - Serve as a trusted advisor to Sales and GTM leadership on where to invest by vertical, with clear recommendations and regular performance reporting. Who you are We're looking for exceptional individuals who combine technical excellence with ethical awareness, who are excited by hard problems and motivated by human impact. matches.d: 1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that. But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens. We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better. About the Team & Role The Rev Ops team at Headway powers our revenue engine by generating insights, building workflows, and running AI-native operations that drive our commercial teams to deliver provider and patient growth at scale This role exists to make our revenue motions deeply automated and continuously optimized. You'll build and ship AI-powered workflows, evaluate and deploy AI-native tools, and partner across our GTM and R&D teams to replace manual effort with intelligent systems that drive growth. About the Role: Kong's IT team is standing up a new capability: a small, specialized group that goes directly into business functions and builds AI into how work gets done. We call them AI Enablement Specialists — and we're looking for a senior practitioner to help lead that effort. This isn't an advisory role. You'll be hands-on with the teams you support, building tools that solve real problems and helping people develop new skills they'll carry forward. The scope is company-wide — Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Legal, Customer Success, and beyond. You'll have the autonomy to prioritize where your time creates the most value, and the backing of IT leadership to get things done. If you've already done this kind of work — transforming how people and teams operate through AI — and you're looking for an environment where you can do it at scale with real ownership, this is the role. What You'll Do: - Spend time inside business teams to understand how they actually work — their tools, processes, pain points, and highest-priority outputs. - Build AI-powered workflows, automations, and custom tools that address real bottlenecks and deliver measurable time savings. - Help team members develop their own AI skills through one-on-one coaching, working sessions, and structured practice — moving them from early experimentation to confident, independent use. - Recognize when a solution built for one team applies to others, and do the work to make it reusable across the organization. - Establish a clear framework for tracking AI adoption progress across business units and report findings to IT leadership on a regular cadence. - Set documentation standards for the team — every tool, workflow, and lesson learned should be captured so it doesn't live only in your head. - Help develop Kong's internal AI governance standards in partnership with IT, Security, and Engineering. - Mentor junior team members and interns, giving them hands-on experience and clear feedback. - Stay current on AI developments and translate what's relevant into practical applications for Kong's business context. What You'll Bring: Minimum Requirements - 5+ years of experience in a technical or cross-functional role that required problem-solving across teams and functions. - A track record of building AI-powered tools, automations, or workflows that changed how real work gets done — with specific examples you can speak to. - Experience helping others develop new technical skills, whether through formal training, one-on-one coaching, or team enablement programs. - Clear, concise communication skills — you can explain a technical concept to someone who's never thought about it before, without talking down to them. - Comfort with ambiguity and self-direction; you don't need a detailed roadmap to know where to start. - Experience working in or with an IT organization, or a comparable role supporting business operations across multiple functions. Preferred Qualifications: - Hands-on experience with AI development platforms and tools such as Claude, Claude Code, MCPs, LLM APIs, custom agent frameworks, or workflow automation platforms. - Background in change management, organizational development, or a large-scale rollout that required bringing skeptical stakeholders along. - Experience in consulting, solutions engineering, or a client-facing technical role where you had to earn trust and deliver results quickly. - Familiarity with the enterprise SaaS tools Kong runs on: Okta, Slack, Google Workspace, Salesforce, Jira, or Freshservice. - Experience creating internal toolkits, playbooks, or training programs that outlived your involvement and were adopted at scale. - Familiarity with Kong Konnect, Kong Gateway, or API management concepts — understanding how APIs and AI models connect will help you build smarter tools. #LI-KH1 About Kong: Kong Inc., the AI Connectivity Company, is building the connectivity layer of AI. Trusted by the Fortune 500® and AI-native startups alike, Kong’s unified API and AI platform enables organizations to secure, manage, accelerate, govern, and monetize the flow of intelligence across APIs and AI traffic — on any model, any cloud. For more information, visit www.konghq.com http://www.konghq.com.

matches.why: Outstanding target title at a fast-growing LLM infrastructure startup, explicitly focused on structuring partnerships into a repeatable product.
matches.d: ABOUT OPENROUTER OpenRouter is the unified interface for LLMs. We route billions of tokens every month, helping developers and enterprises access, manage, and optimize their AI use across 400+ models and providers — without worrying about lock-in, capacity constraints, downtime, or complex integrations. Our provider ecosystem is the foundation of that marketplace. As the number of model labs and inference providers we work with grows, the relationships behind them have to scale like a product — with consistent tiers, lifecycles, and standards — not as a set of one-off deals. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Program Manager to turn our Provider Program into a product. Today, provider relationships are managed one at a time; your job is to give them a repeatable structure so the ecosystem scales without adding headcount for every new partner. You’ll own the standard provider lifecycle end to end — sourcing, onboarding, activation, QBR, and renewal — along with provider tiering (our “buckets”), SLAs, and the compliance cadence that keeps the program trustworthy. You’ll be the one person with context across every partnership, able to run program-wide operations (re-paper all providers, roll out a new compliance attestation, launch a new tier) without pulling individual partnership owners off their accounts. You’ll also run our flagship programs, starting with MPEAP (Model Provider Early Access Program) and our verified/certified provider tracks. This is a high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Security. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own the provider lifecycle. Define and operate the standard path from sourcing → onboarding → activation → QBR → renewal, with clear stage gates, owners, and SLAs. - Design provider tiering. Build and maintain the tiering framework (the “buckets”) that determines how providers are classified, what they get, and what’s expected of them. - Build programmatic structure that scales. Turn one-off relationships into repeatable systems — templates, playbooks, self-serve onboarding, and automated provider comms — so the program grows without linear headcount. - Run cross-program operations. Execute program-wide changes (re-paper all providers, launch a new tier, roll out a new compliance attestation) as a single coordinated motion. - Run the flagship programs. Operate MPEAP and the verified/certified provider tracks, from intake criteria to ongoing management. - Own the compliance cadence. Keep SLAs, attestations, and provider obligations on schedule and auditable. - Set the operating cadence. Run the rhythm of the team — reviews, reporting, and the operating cadence that keeps everyone aligned. - Partner cross-functionally. Work across Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Security to unblock providers and ship program improvements. ABOUT YOU - Programs + strategy background. You’ve built and run programs or strategy at a large, complex organization (e.g. a Salesforce-scale org) and know how to impose structure on ambiguity. - Highly organized systems thinker. You instinctively turn recurring work into repeatable, automatable processes and see where linear effort should become leverage. - Cross-functional operator. You’re comfortable owning operations that span Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Security, and driving them to closure without formal authority. - High agency and bias to ship. You take end-to-end ownership, move fast, and thrive in a small, fast-moving team with intentionally fluid boundaries. - Strong written communication. You can turn complex, multi-stakeholder programs into clear docs, playbooks, and comms. - Bonus: familiarity with the AI ecosystem — model labs, inference providers, and what it takes to onboard and certify them. WHAT WE OFFER - A front-row seat to the AI ecosystem and direct relationships with the model labs and providers shaping it. - High ownership and the room to define a program from the ground up. - Remote-first (US), competitive salary and equity, fully covered health/dental/vision, unlimited PTO, a WFH budget, and quarterly offsites. If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria above but are still interested in the role, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we’re looking for someone excited to build this program with us.

matches.d: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. About the Role Skydio is seeking a Readiness Specialist to get our dock customers from signed opportunity to a running program. You will own a book of accounts within a region, from large cities to small towns, and project manage each customer through everything that has to be true before a dock flies: the site, the network, the policy and approvals behind the program, the flight operation that will run it, and a clean handoff to Customer Success. Most of that work is done by other people, inside the customer and inside Skydio, and none of them report to you. The job is building the relationships that get it done, and holding the date. This is a remote role. Travel of 50 to 60% is required to support site surveys, customer engagements, deployments, team onsites, and company events. About the Team The Launch Team is the operational arm of Skydio's dock business. We sit between the opportunity and the running program, and readiness means everything a customer needs to launch. We do not perform every piece of that work, but we project manage the customer to all of it and are accountable for the date. Readiness starts before the contract is signed. Much of it runs on calendar time Skydio does not control, such as an engineering study, a purchase order, or an MOU in legal review, so the earlier it starts, the sooner the dock is in the ground. The team is measured on time-to-launch, readiness gate adherence, deployment schedule performance, and the condition of the program at handoff. Readiness Specialists are critical members of the Skydio organization and work closely with Account Executives, Solutions Engineers, Deployment Engineering, Integrations, and Customer Success to support successful deployments, customer confidence, and the long-term success of dock programs. How You’ll Make an Impact - Own a book of dock accounts within your region and run the weekly customer cadence, readiness record, and risk tracking on every one, from opportunity through clean handoff to Customer Success. - Build the working relationships that move a launch: the customer's program manager, facilities and IT staff, procurement, and legal on the outside, and Account Executives, Solutions Engineers, Deployment, and Customer Success on the inside. - Lead site surveys and make-ready planning, including rooftop and site assessments, power and mounting, and RF, LTE, and network readiness with the customer's IT and network administrators. - Drive the non-technical path to launch: waivers and BVLOS approvals, policy and data retention, council or board authorization, and pilot staffing and training. Name that work for the customer early so it does not surprise them later. - Hold the line on readiness gates. Deployment prerequisites are verified before a dock ships, and when an account goes dark or a blocker exceeds your authority, escalate early through the AE, SE, or leader who can clear it. - Cover for other specialists in your region during absence or surge, and turn what you see across launches into playbook improvements and prioritized, defensible feedback for Product and Engineering. What Makes You a Good Fit - 3+ years in a customer-facing project management, implementation, deployment, or operations role. - Experience managing a portfolio of concurrent projects with timelines, dependencies, and outside stakeholders you do not control. - Familiarity with Drone as First Responder concepts of operation and dock based remote operations. Professional experience is strongly preferred. - Comfort working with public sector and enterprise customers, including their IT, facilities, procurement, and legal teams. - Highly organized with strong attention to detail, and disciplined about keeping the system of record current. - Excellent written and verbal communication. You can brief an operator, a program manager, and a chief or a city council without changing the facts. Nice to Have - Prior public safety service, or experience standing up a Drone as First Responder program on the agency side. - Experience supporting an agency through a public approval process, such as council or board authorization, public comment, or privacy and data retention policy. - Familiarity with site survey, RF and LTE assessment, and network readiness for fixed installations. - Familiarity with grant funding pathways and cooperative purchasing vehicles used by state and local agencies. - Working knowledge of Salesforce, Palantir, Databricks, or equivalents. What Is Required - FAA Part 107 Certificate, or the ability to obtain one within 60 days of hire. - Ability to travel 50 to 60% of the time. - Ability to lift up to 60 lbs unaided. - Comfortable working outdoors, at height, and performing physical tasks including climbing ladders. Compensation: At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual salary range for this position is $125,000 - $170,000*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria. *Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position’s location. #LI-AY1 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. matches.d: About the company In the coming decades, demand for critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt will continue to grow. These minerals are needed to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. However, the mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered. KoBold was founded to be the first AI native mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects. Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations. KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery. KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi. About the position In this role, you will report to a Lead or Manager within the Commercial Analytics team, and work closely within a remote team of 5 - 7 (across North America and Europe) to structure ambiguous problems, build financial and operational models, and provide recommendations to the C-suite for key decisions. The work will span a variety of topics and include traditional market analyses such as creating supply/demand forecasts and writing commodity outlook reports, and non-traditional analyses as-needed to advance KoBold’s mission – e.g., operational and financial modeling for KoBold’s exploration programs, build vs. buy decisions for KoBold’s technology, mine economics modeling, and scientific communication materials for external audiences s, to name a few. This is an ideal role for a recent graduate looking to acquire a wide range of skills very quickly. The learning curve will be steep, and the work will be varied and intellectually demanding. Responsibilities The Commercial & Scientific Analyst/Lead will: Aggregate existing research and/or conduct original research to build forecasts and models related to commodity markets, KoBold operations, mine development, and more Work with the Commercial Analytics and Financial Planning & Analysis team to answer strategic questions from leadership Prepare materials for the Board of Directors and investors or partners Use a first-principles approach in collaboration with various KoBold functions to help make decisions or improve operational efficiency (e.g., cost models for technology, HR, exploration programs, carbon emissions reporting, trade-off/sensitivity analyses) Conduct analytics for critical workstreams in mine development and exploration Build and maintain financial models assessing project economics Support others on the Commercial Analytics team on various analytical assignments Qualifications A great candidate will have: Education in a STEM discipline or economics (physics, chemistry, astronomy/astrophysics, or mathematics is preferred) At least 1 year of experience in technology, natural resources, finance, or professional services Experience with Python or other scientific computing language and/or financial modeling Excitement about working on a wide array of problems Excellent communication and organizational skills Regardless of formal training, a strong orientation toward thinking from first principles with respect to science, technology, economics, and business Work practices and motivation: Demonstrated ability to quickly absorb and synthesize complex information, with a keen eye for detail and intellectual rigor Exceptional curiosity and eagerness to learn, with a proactive approach to exploring new concepts and technologies Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on a range of responsibilities Ability to independently prioritize multiple tasks effectively What to Expect Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. matches.d: About Phaidra Phaidra is building the future of industrial automation. The world today is filled with static, monolithic infrastructure. Factories, power plants, buildings, etc. operate the same they've operated for decades — because the controls programming is hard-coded. Thousands of lines of rules and heuristics that define how the machines interact with each other. The result of all this hard-coding is that facilities are frozen in time, unable to adapt to their environment while their performance slowly degrades. Phaidra creates AI-powered control systems for the industrial sector, enabling industrial facilities to automatically learn and improve over time. Specifically: We use reinforcement learning algorithms to provide this intelligence, converting raw sensor data into high-value actions and decisions. We focus on industrial applications, which tend to be well-sensorized with measurable KPIs — perfect for reinforcement learning. We enable domain experts (our users) to configure the AI control systems (i.e. agents) without writing code. They define what they want their AI agents to do, and we do it for them. Our team has a track record of applying AI to some of the toughest problems. From achieving superhuman performance with DeepMind's AlphaGo , to reducing the energy required to cool Google's Data Centers by 40%, we deeply understand AI and how to apply it in production for massive impact. Phaidra’s ability to achieve its mission is determined by our ability to work together — as defined by our core values: Transparency , Collaboration , Operational Excellence , Ownership , and Empathy. We seek individuals who embody these values, as they are instrumental in ensuring our team consistently delivers excellence and fosters an engaging and supportive culture Phaidra is based in the USA, but we are 100% remote with no physical office. We hire employees internationally with the help of our partner, OysterHR . Our team is currently located throughout the USA, Canada, UK, Sweden, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, Singapore, Australia, and India. Who you are You’re an independent worker, skilled in organization, planning, and project management. You have technical knowledge of industrial controls, building automation systems, and/or air or water cooled chiller plants. You have the drive to learn about different industries and technologies, and a passion to help customers operate their plant more efficiently and effectively with Phaidra’s AI supervisory control system. You can take ownership of your assigned customers and delight them! You can guide internal and external teams as you coordinate the configuration and installation of the customers industrial plant AI Agents, and provide professional support while you grow customer relationships for future expansion and advocacy. You thrive in a process-driven environment, yet possess the flexibility to adapt and tailor those processes to each customer's unique needs. You enjoy collaborating with cross-functional teams to tackle complex projects, leveraging your expertise to drive successful outcomes. **This role is posted at multiple levels (mid-level and senior). Final leveling, title, and compensation will be determined based on the candidate's experience, skills, and qualifications during the interview process. Responsibilities Own end-to-end delivery of complex, large-scale customer programs, including multi-site, multi-product, and highly customized deployments, ensuring successful execution from kickoff through long-term support and customer satisfaction. Lead program strategy and planning by defining timelines, milestones, resource allocation, and risk mitigation plans across concurrent initiatives, aligning execution with both customer goals and company objectives. Serve as the primary customer-facing program leader and trusted advisor, proactively guiding customers through technical and operational challenges while delivering strategic recommendations. Work closely with engineering and product teams to ensure our customer solutions are configured correctly and delivered on time according to the customer’s specific site requirements. Independently manage high-complexity engagements, navigating ambiguity, prioritizing competing demands, and ensuring consistent delivery against scope, schedule, and quality expectations. Lead executive-level communication, presenting complex technical concepts, program updates, and risks in a clear, concise, and actionable manner to stakeholders at all levels. Proactively identify program risks, inefficiencies or gaps in delivery workflows, and lead initiatives to update playbooks or processes that improve delivery, customer experience, and internal operations. Shape and influence customer strategy by aligning evolving customer needs with long-term product and company direction, providing structured feedback to inform product development. Establish and continuously improve program management best practices, including documentation standards, onboarding processes, and delivery frameworks. Own comprehensive program documentation, including project progress milestone records, critical customer decisions, technical requirements, and customer-facing materials. Lead complex internal initiatives that enhance product capabilities, deployment methodologies, or operational tooling. Peer-mentor other TPMs on project execution and technical domain nuances; provide 'on-the-job' guidance during onboarding to help new hires navigate internal processes and manage their first customer deployments Adapt and apply appropriate project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, hybrid approaches) based on program complexity and customer requirements. Uses AI tools strategically to accelerate delivery, improve quality, and guide others in effective AI-assisted workflows. Key Qualifications 5+ years of technical program or project management experience, with demonstrated ownership of complex, cross-functional initiatives. Proven ability to independently lead large-scale, technically complex customer programs with high levels of ambiguity. Strong experience working with enterprise customers and distributed, cross-functional teams. Exceptional ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, including executive stakeholders. Demonstrated experience in stakeholder management, risk management, and program execution at scale. Ability to translate explicit and implicit customer needs into structured requirements and influence product and engineering roadmaps. Demonstrated expertise in at least two of the following domains, with working proficiency across others: Data centers Industrial controls and automation systems HVAC and mission-critical cooling systems AI / Machine Learning applications in industrial environments Proficiency in a wide range of program management tools and methodologies, including Agile, Waterfall, and risk management frameworks. Strong documentation and organizational skills with a focus on creating scalable, repeatable processes. Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience. Preferred Skills & Experience Strong track record of driving process improvements and operational excellence initiatives. Experience leading cross-functional technical solution delivery involving engineering, research, and product teams. Proven ability to mentor, coach, and develop team members. Experience influencing product strategy through customer insights and program learnings. Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent. Onboarding In your first 30 days… You will be immersed in an onboarding program that introduces you to Phaidra and our product. You will read various parts of our handbook and familiarize yourself with the documentation culture at Phaidra. You will join calls with current customers to familiarize yourself with managing customer installs. You will familiarize yourself with our tools and process for developing customer schedules. You will meet with members of the Customer Success department to better understand strengths and opportunities with current processes. By your first 60 days… You will have a solid understanding of what Phaidra does and how deliver for customers. You will have met with team members across Phaidra and started building relationships that will help you be successful at your job. You will have become proficient at navigating the department’s processes and software tools. You will learn how to manage customer support issues and assist with managing our customer service agreements. You will assist in creating and managing project and process documentation. By your first 90 days… You will have been fully integrated into the Customer Success team and with Phaidra team members across the company. You will have begun to manage your own customers and projects. You will help improve our processes and project documentation.
